technology: Three new combined-cycle combustion turbine plants
caveat: The 2,260 MW is the combined nameplate capacity of three utility-owned plants Entergy will build on its own system, not a block of capacity sold to Meta under a contract; Entergy has not disclosed how much of the output Meta pays for or on what terms. The Louisiana Public Service Commission approved the certification in August 2025, which is why the row is marked permitted rather than announced.

technology: Combined-cycle gas plant (Delta Blues Advanced Power Station)
caveat: Entergy names no data-center customer in this release, so the link to any specific hyperscaler is reporting rather than disclosure. The 754 MW is the plant's rating, serving Entergy Mississippi's whole system; no contracted volume to a data center has been published.

technology: Seven GE Vernova gas turbines on a former coal site
caveat: This is a generation build, not a signed supply contract: no data-center tenant or offtaker is named, and "up to 4.5 GW" is the planned plant capacity rather than capacity anybody has agreed to buy. First turbine deliveries were expected to begin in 2026.

technology: Gas redevelopment of the former Bruce Mansfield coal plant
caveat: No capacity was disclosed for the new Shippingport plant, so this row carries no megawatt figure. The only capacity numbers in the announcement are the 2.7 GW rating of the retired coal plant and a statement that more than one gigawatt of surplus would go back to PJM; the co-located data-center partner is unnamed.

technology: Restart of Three Mile Island Unit 1 (Crane Clean Energy Center)
caveat: The 835 MW is the carbon-free energy Constellation says the restart would add to the grid, not a metered flow to any Microsoft building; the unit last operated at 837 MW before its 2019 shutdown. Restart depends on regulatory approvals and grid work, and the plant was still not generating as of this check.

technology: Restart of the Duane Arnold Energy Center boiling water reactor
caveat: The plant has been shut down since 2020 and nothing is being delivered yet; NextEra targets grid delivery by the first quarter of 2029. The 615 MW is the unit's rating, and Google is one of two buyers named, with a rural cooperative taking the remainder.

technology: Fleet of Gen IV fluoride salt-cooled advanced reactors
caveat: This is a master plant development agreement setting up a path to 500 MW by 2035, not a set of executed power purchase agreements; individual PPAs and sites were left to be signed later. No state or specific plant was named at announcement.

technology: Hermes 2 advanced reactor demonstration plant
caveat: TVA, not Google, is the contracting purchaser; Google takes the clean-energy attributes and the power reaches its Tennessee and Alabama data centers through TVA's grid. The 50 MW is an "up to" figure from a demonstration reactor that is not yet generating, with operations expected in 2030.

technology: Xe-100 high-temperature gas-cooled small modular reactors
caveat: The 320 MW is the four-unit first project with Energy Northwest, the only sized commitment in the announcement; the wider "more than 5 gigawatts by 2039" is a collaboration target with no projects or contracts attached. Amazon's role here is partly equity: it anchored a roughly $500 million financing round.

technology: Aurora powerhouse fast reactors
caveat: Oklo describes this as a non-binding master power agreement running through 2044, with binding PPAs to follow as milestones are met, so the 12 GW is an ambition rather than contracted capacity. No sites, dates or first-project size were named, and Oklo had no reactor in operation at announcement.

technology: Aurora powerhouse fast reactors
caveat: Meta states "up to 1.2 GW" at a Pike County, Ohio site with power as early as 2030, so the figure is a ceiling on a project that has not been licensed or built. Oklo had no operating reactor when this was announced.

technology: Natrium sodium-cooled reactors with integrated thermal storage
caveat: The 2.8 GW is baseload generation capacity across a multi-unit programme stretching to 2035, separate from 1.2 GW of built-in storage; only up to 690 MW has a near-term delivery date, as early as 2032. No sites were named and no Natrium unit is operating.

technology: Small modular reactor at the North Anna site
caveat: A memorandum of understanding to explore feasibility, with no capacity, price or commitment to build disclosed by either company. Figures of at least 300 MW circulate in coverage of Amazon's wider SMR programme but do not appear in this joint announcement.

technology: Coal and oil units kept online under reliability-must-run terms
source_name: Talen Energy press release filed with the SEC
caveat: No data center is a party to this: it is a settlement among Talen, PJM, Maryland regulators and others that keeps Brandon Shores and H.A. Wagner running to 31 May 2029 while Baltimore-area transmission is upgraded. Talen disclosed the payment rates, $312/MW-day and $137/MW-day, but not the megawatts covered, so the capacity field is left empty.

technology: Coal units at Plants Bowen and Scherer kept in operation
caveat: This is a state resource-plan approval, not a contract with any data center: the 4,000 MW is the capacity of coal units whose operation is extended through at least 2034, and none of it is assigned to a named customer. Georgia Power's own filings note its data-center load forecasts carry significant potential for overestimation.

technology: Behind-the-meter gas turbines co-located with the data center
source_name: Chevron press release filed with the SEC
caveat: Chevron describes 2.67 GW of behind-the-meter power under a 20-year agreement, but the plant is not built and a final investment decision was still expected by the end of 2026. The capacity is to be phased in modules rather than delivered at once.

technology: 29 LM2500XPRESS aeroderivative gas turbine packages
caveat: This is an equipment order, not a power contract, and GE Vernova gave only a rounded figure, "nearly 1 GW" across the 29 units, so no capacity is recorded here. No site or state is named in the announcement, and the two tranches were booked in December 2024 and June 2025.

technology: 15 Solar SMT-130 gas turbines at the Colossus site
source_name: TechCrunch, reporting the Shelby County Health Department permit
caveat: The 247 MW is the ceiling written into an air permit, not a contracted supply or a measured output, and the permit treats the units as backup with strict annual run-hour limits. xAI has published nothing itself, and the permit was under appeal by community groups.

technology: Distributed gas turbines supplying primary on-site power
source_name: Solaris Energy Infrastructure press release filed with the SEC
caveat: Solaris names only "a major data center client" and no site or state, so the buyer side of this row is a description rather than a name. The roughly 900 MW is the upsized contract size, up from 500 MW, over an initial seven-year term, and the equipment was still being delivered.

technology: Solid oxide fuel cells co-located at data-center sites
caveat: The gigawatt is the ceiling of a supply agreement, not equipment ordered: only 100 MW was firmly ordered at announcement, with further orders left to 2025. AEP is a utility buying the hardware, so the eventual data-center customers were not named and no site or state was given.

technology: Solid oxide fuel cells for on-site data-center power
caveat: The 1.2 GW is the portion actually contracted and being deployed; the headline 2.8 GW is what Oracle "intends to procure" under a master services agreement and is not itself an order. Bloom names no individual sites beyond saying the projects are in the United States.

technology: Solid oxide fuel cells for AI data-center campuses
caveat: The only number attached to this partnership is an investment commitment of up to $5 billion, so no fuel-cell capacity is recorded; dollars are not megawatts. The scope is global rather than United States only, and the first named site under discussion was in Europe.

technology: Long-duration CO2 battery storage
caveat: A global commercial framework with a strategic investment attached, carrying no disclosed capacity, no named projects and no United States site at announcement. Storage shifts energy in time rather than adding supply, so nothing here is new generation for a data center.

technology: 19 MW, 10-hour CO2 battery at the Coronado Generating Station
caveat: Google's role is cost-sharing to help a utility adopt non-lithium storage, not an offtake agreement, and the output is dispatched by Salt River Project onto its grid rather than routed to a Google building. The project is small by data-center standards and is not expected online until 2029.

technology: Second-life EV battery microgrid with solar
caveat: At 12 MW and 63 MWh this powers a modular container-scale deployment, not a hyperscale campus, and the batteries store solar output rather than generate. The companies describe it as the largest second-life battery installation of its kind, which is a claim about reuse rather than about scale.

technology: Existing nuclear output from the Susquehanna plant
source_name: Talen Energy press release filed with the SEC
caveat: Nothing new is built here: Susquehanna already runs, and the agreement re-papers an existing 2.5 GW plant's output as a front-of-meter supply to Amazon through 2042. The full 1,920 MW is not flowing today, with the ramp expected to complete no later than 2032.

technology: Existing nuclear output from the Clinton Clean Energy Center
caveat: This buys the output of a plant that already exists and keeps it running after Illinois ratepayer credits expire; deliveries do not begin until June 2027. Only 30 MW of the total is new energy, coming from planned uprates.

technology: Existing nuclear output from the Comanche Peak plant
source_name: World Nuclear News, quoting Vistra's fourth-quarter 2025 results call
caveat: Vistra's own filing of 29 September 2025 described the counterparty only as a large investment-grade company; the chief executive named Amazon Web Services months later on an earnings call. The 1,200 MW is an "up to" figure from an existing plant, with deliveries beginning in the fourth quarter of 2027 and reaching full volume by 2032.

technology: Existing nuclear output from the Perry and Davis-Besse plants
caveat: Meta describes "more than 2.1 GW" from two plants that already operate, so the figure here is the lower bound of that phrasing; Vistra later put the contracted total at 2,176 MW. A further 433 MW of uprates across Perry, Davis-Besse and Beaver Valley in Pennsylvania is contracted separately and is not counted in this row.

technology: New wind and solar capacity under a global framework
caveat: The 10.5 GW spans the United States and Europe, so only part of it belongs to American data centers, and it is a five-year framework for development rather than a set of signed project contracts. Capacity is meant to be delivered between 2026 and 2030, with no projects named at announcement.

technology: Solar and wind power purchase agreements
caveat: These are grid-connected projects in Ohio, Arkansas and Texas whose output Meta buys on paper; the electricity does not travel to a particular building, and the sites do not sit next to Meta's data centers. None was operating at announcement, with commercial operation expected in 2027 and 2028.

technology: Enhanced geothermal generation at Cape Station
caveat: Deliveries are not expected until 2028 from a project still being drilled, and an optional expansion of roughly 600 MW is not contracted. Enhanced geothermal at this scale has no long operating record, so the 396 MW is a contracted volume rather than demonstrated output.

technology: Enhanced geothermal supplied through the Clean Transition Tariff
caveat: Google does not buy this power directly: NV Energy takes the geothermal output from Fervo's Corsac Station project and Google pays a tariff premium covering the gap against the cheaper resource the utility would otherwise have built. Nevada regulators approved the structure in May 2025 and the plant was not yet generating.

technology: Water-independent next-generation geothermal
caveat: The 150 MW is split across two phases, a small first phase and a larger second one, with both only projected to be operational by 2030 and neither sized publicly. Power goes onto the PNM grid rather than to a Meta facility directly, and XGS had no plant of this size in operation.

technology: Co-located renewables and storage in industrial energy parks
caveat: No capacity was disclosed, only an intention to build gigawatts of co-located data-center and clean-power capacity, so this row carries no megawatt figure. Google's role is described as anchor offtaker plus investor, and no site, state or first-project size was named.
